A Django **app** is one of the loosely‑coupled components that make up a Django project.  In the framework, each component can be managed independently, which lets you separate concerns such as data storage, request handling, and presentation [3].  An app packages a specific piece of functionality—its own models, templates, and views—so you can reuse it in multiple projects or replace it without affecting the rest of the codebase.  

The textbook points out that you will learn the difference between Django **projects** (the overall site configuration) and **applications**, which are the building blocks you assemble inside a project [4].  Because apps follow Django’s MTV (Model‑Template‑View) pattern, they contain the three layers needed to handle data, render HTML, and respond to web requests [3].  This modular design supports rapid development and code reusability, core goals of Django [1][3].
